title: Minimum Window Substring
description: Find the smallest substring of s containing every character of t, using a variable window with a satisfiability counter.

data.text: Given strings `s` and `t`, return the **shortest substring of `s`** that contains every character of `t`, including duplicates. If no such substring exists, return the empty string.

**Input:** `s = "ADOBECODEBANC"`, `t = "ABC"`

**Output:** `"BANC"`

**Explanation:** `"BANC"` contains A, B, and C and is shorter than `"ADOBEC"` and `"CODEBA"`.

Count the characters `t` requires. Slide a window over `s`, expanding on the right until the window contains every required character, then shrink from the left for as long as it stays valid. Track the shortest valid window seen. Because `left` and `right` each travel from 0 to n once, the total cost is O(n).
Approach: Two Counters and a Satisfiability Score

Comparing two full dictionaries on every window step costs O(alphabet) per step. Instead track how many **distinct characters** are currently satisfied. The window is complete when `satisfied == required`. This keeps each step O(1).

data.title: Sliding Window O(n)
data.content: Expand until satisfied, then shrink while still satisfied.

data.title: Equality, not greater-than
data.text: Increment `satisfied` only when the count reaches the requirement *exactly* (`window[c] == needed`). If you increment whenever `window[c] >= needed`, the same character gets counted multiple times and the window is declared complete too early, producing a wrong (usually too-short) answer.

data.title: Shrink with a while, expand with a for
data.text: This expand-then-shrink structure is the general template for all 'minimum window satisfying a constraint' problems. Replace the satisfiability check and the same code solves 'longest repeating character replacement' and 'minimum size subarray sum'.

data.caption: The window expands until it contains A, B and C, then contracts from the left until it would break the requirement.
data.definition:
graph TD
    A["s = ADOBECODEBANC, t = ABC"] --> B["expand to ADOBEC: satisfied = 3"]
    B --> C["shrink: DOBEC, OBEC, BEC (invalid)"]
    C --> D["BEC len 3 -> resume expanding"]
    D --> E["expand to BANC: satisfied = 3"]
    E --> F["shrink: ANC, NC (invalid)"]
    F --> G["best = BANC len 4"]
    style G fill:#e8f5e9,stroke:#2e7d32

data.title: Complete solution
data.content: The satisfiability counter is what makes this O(n): without it, checking 'does the window contain all of t' costs O(alphabet) on every step. Remember to count duplicates in `t` correctly — an input of `"AABC"` requires two A's.
